_note: SL-098 review m2, closed as a class: a PowerShell function whose caller uses its return value, and that writes to the success stream inside. Its members come from a script author calling, in such a function, something that prints: one of this file's own reporting functions (Check and the ones that call it), a cmdlet whose default output is an object (New-Item), Write-Output and its aliases, or a script block called through & whose output nobody has seen. The value then arrives as an array of the printed text and the value, or the printed text is captured by the caller and never shown, and either way nothing complains: a Join-Path on the array stops a case, a FAIL line is counted and never printed. 'census' is closed: every function in tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1, nested ones included, has one row, as 'returns' (a caller uses its value), 'neither' (a caller uses nothing, but it must be as silent as a returning function, since it runs inside one) or 'emits' (it writes to the success stream by design, and is where its callers must not look for a value); the test fails on a function with no row and on a row with no function. A returning or silent function may call an emitting one, a cmdlet in 'outputting', or a script block through &, only where the output is consumed: assigned, cast to void, piped to a sink, redirected to $null, or the argument of another command. 'plants' feeds the checker one function each, fire or quiet, so it is shown able to tell. 'dynamic' runs the real functions (RuleCases.ps1 taken through the parser) and counts what they put in the pipeline. The code before the review fix (a Write-Output in New-TempDir, no Out-Host at the Invoke-HarnessRaw call of Remove-ScratchDir, none on its early return, none on the & $change call) fails the rows named in 'before'.
